The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,

Commissioner Barragan, Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, Vice
Chair Apodaca, and Chair Lopez. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of

Deputy City Attorney (participated remotely); and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative
Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of September 24, 2025.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2023-06
Ben Martin (“Applicant”) on behalf of Rexford Industrial Realty LP; a request to demolish
two existing multi-tenant industrial warehouse buildings totaling 89,870 SF to construct a
new 138,972± SF industrial warehouse building with off-street parking, landscaping
improvements, and associated infrastructure on a 7.03-acre lot located at 14830
Carmenita Road (APN: 8069-002-085). The proposed building would include 132,227 SF
of warehouse space, 3,715 SF of ground-floor office space, and 3,030 SF of mezzanine
office space.
Environmental: Review and adoption of Mitigated Negative Declaration with the Mitigation
Monitoring and Reporting Plan.

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Development Services Manager
Lee presented a report stating that the request is to demolish two existing industrial
buildings totaling 89,870 square feet and construct a new 138,972 square foot industrial
warehouse building and associated improvements on a 7.03 acre lot located at 14830
Carmenita Road; that the site is zoned Heavy Industrial by the General Plan; that
approximately 132,227 square feet of floor area will be utilized as warehouse space,
3,715 square feet will be used as a ground-floor office, and about 3,030 square feet will
be utilized for mezzanine office space; that the development will provide 141 off-street
parking spaces, 22 loading dock doors, and 8 bicycle racks, as well as a trash enclosure;
that the building is designed in a contemporary warehouse style with varying roof lines;
that in staff’s analysis of the project, they did find that the project is consistent with the
General Plan Land Use Element objective in that it would maintain a high caliber of
industrial development by providing for the improvement of existing industrial properties;
that the proposed project will have a positive impact on the surrounding neighborhood,
redevelop an existing industrial site and improve the economic vitality of the site; and that
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 8, 2025

new landscape improvements and architectural building treatments will enhance the
overall area.

Continuing with her presentation, Development Services Manager Lee commented on
the environmental analysis required. She indicated that the Initial Study and Mitigated
Negative Declaration was initially circulated for this project on October 24, 2024 until
November 12, 2024; that during the public review period, public comments were received
from the Los Angeles County Sanitation District and from Adams Broadwell Joseph &
Cardozo who also provided public comments which have been addressed and
incorporated in the Initial Study (IS) Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and related
Mitigation Monitoring Reporting Program (MMRP); that pursuant to the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the IS/MND was recirculated for a secondary public
review period beginning on September 12, 2025 and ended on October 1, 2025; that the
purpose of the recirculation was to clarify the construction stages for the project, which
include crushing as part of demolition activities; addressing revisions to Air Quality and
Health Risk Assessment in response to public comments received on the original Draft
IS/MND; addresses the request for mitigation received from the Gabrieleno Band of
Mission Indians-Kizh Nation; that, to date, one comment has been received from the Los
Angeles County Sheriff’s Department; and that, essentially, the environmental factors
have been updated.

Further, Ms. Lee stated that the conditions of approval for this project include approval
for two years, with two one-year extensions approved by the Director, and a final one-
year extension by the Planning Commission; that a maximum of 21,735 square feet of
the floor area may be used for cold storage; that a maximum 20 percent of the floor area
may be designated for General Light Industrial; that the mitigation measures address
the following: air quality, cultural resources, energy, geology and soils, hazards and
hazardous materials, hydrology and water quality, noise, public services, tribal cultural
resources and utilities; that a letter of concern was received from Adams Broadwell
Joseph & Cardozo on behalf of the Coalition for Responsible Equitable Economic
Development (“CREED LA”) which was forwarded to the Planning Commission; and
that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission (1) Adopt the Mitigated
Negative Declaration with the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plan (MMRP)
contained therein; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 25-13, to approve Precise
Development Plan (PDP) No. 2023-06 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained
in Exhibit “A” and the MMRP contained in Exhibit “B”.

The applicant’s representative, Brandon Wolfe, stated that the last time he was before
the Commission was in December 2024, at which time they requested a continuance to
allow them to address some concerns on the environmental document; that staff did an
excellent job with this project; that, for the record, he would like to reiterate Rexford
Industrial’s goals and how they operate as a business; that the subject site is currently
occupied by two industrial buildings, approximately 90,000 square feet; that their intention
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 8, 2025

is to redevelop that property with a 138,000 square foot single tenant Class A warehouse
facility; that Rexford, as a company, typically pursues LEED certification which has stricter
requirements; that this applies to all of their properties throughout Southern California,
including the subject project; that by the time they go through their plan check process
the 2026 California Building Code updates will apply; that they have not officially
completed plan check construction drawings; and that all the departments will be
reviewing those plans and any updates that may occur within the next twelve months.

Jeffery Rivera stated that he is a Level 2 apprentice with Laborers Local 1309 LiUNA; that
he wants to have a stable income to support his future family the same way his father has
been providing for them for 15 years; that he is hoping to graduate from his apprenticeship
program and work at the Carmenita Road Industrial warehouse; and that he and his fellow
union members who are in the audience tonight are in full support of this project.

Jose Radillo provided testimony in support of the request. He stated that this project
creates jobs and that it will be built to higher standards by union labor; and that he hopes
that the Commission supports the applicant’s request.

Aidan Marshall stated that he is speaking on behalf of CREED LA; that they are
requesting that the Commission continue this hearing for a full environmental impact
report as required by CEQA; that CEQA requires an EIR as opposed to a Mitigated
Negative Declaration whenever there is substantial evidence that there may be potentially
significant environmental impacts such as air quality, public housing issues,
transportation, and public utilities; that this clearly triggers the preparation of an EIR under
the law; that regarding transportation, their transportation expert looked at the numbers
and found that the city is overestimating the existing trips from the existing use, and under-
estimating the trips from the proposed use; and that due to the aforementioned reasons
they are requesting that the Commission continue the hearing for the preparation of an
Environmental Impact Report.

Meaghan Truman, EPD Solutions, Inc., stated that they prepared the environmental
document for the project; that, essentially, the comments made by Mr. Marshall do not
provide substantial evidence of a fair argument for an Environmental Impact Report; that
all the comments relied on either inaccurate information, argument or speculation; that
regarding the comment that air quality would have a cumulative impact; that based on the
Air Quality Management District (AQMD) threshold referred to, those figures are not
actually a published or adopted threshold; that regarding transportation and that the trips
were overestimated, the trips are based on the existing uses on site, which is warehousing
and storage; and that the comment provided as far as overestimating the current trips is
based on argument.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed the
public hearing.

Commissioner Barragan indicated that her questions have been answered.

Commissioner Macias stated that his concern is with the truck routes and that they do not
impact the area schools.

Alex Garber, EPD Solutions, Inc. stated that they analyzed the truck routes from the
Circulation Element; that the trucks are primarily heading south on Carmenita to the
freeway interchange, and that this would have a less than significant impact on schools.

In response to Commissioner Vernola-Salas’ question who is going to be responsible for
maintaining the streets as there is going to be more truck traffic, Mr. Wolfe indicated that
the applicant pays development impact fees to the city’s general funds for maintenance
of city right-of-way roads; that they will also be contributing fees to the School District;
that anything pertaining to private property and owned by Rexford Industrial for this site
will be maintained by Rexford Industrial; and that they have an in-house property
management firm that handles any issues pertaining to their site.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas asked if the warehouse is going to be a 24-hour operation,
Mr. Wolfe indicated that it is a 24-hour, 7-day operation; that the truck traffic, generally
speaking, occurs during city ordinance hours; that there may be one or two trucks that
come in late at night, handled by a skeleton crew; that Excelsior is the main point of entry;
that they have a Reciprocal Access agreement with the property to the left that already
utilizes Carmenita Road; that should access be needed they would record a CC&R with
the western property; however, truck traffic would be southbound to get to the closest
onramp to the freeway.

Vice Chair Apodaca stated that they are tearing down two warehouses and building a
new one with 22 dock doors; that this is not that large of an operation; that the subject
site is a prime location for warehousing and transportation being so close to the freeway
and being in an industrial area, and that the use will not have a big impact on the area.

Mr. Wolfe shared that the applicant is specializing in looking for underutilized properties
to redevelop and improve the character of that area; that they are not looking for any
discretionary action regarding the subject site; that the intention is to revitalize the area
with a Class A facility; and that they do not envision that the project will be generating too
much additional traffic.

Interim Director Hamilton stated that to address the comment made regarding
maintenance of the public right-of-way, Condition of Approval Numbers 22 and 27
addresses those concerns.

Planning Commissioner Vernola-Salas stated that her main concern is with Excelsior.

Mr. Wolfe stated that during the construction plan check process and tenant occupancy
process there will be another set of eyes as far as who is going to be operating and
utilizing the facility.

It was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Barragan to: (1)
Adopt the Mitigated Negative Declaration with the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
Plan (MMRP) contained therein; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 25-13, to approve
Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2023-06 subject to the Conditions of Approval
contained in Exhibit “A” and the MMRP contained in Exhibit “B”.

SUBJECT:  Zoning Text Amendment No. 2025-01 to amend various sections of Title 17
  of the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) as it relates to residential

Authority:

Section 65855 of the California Government Code states that the Planning Commission
shall make a written recommendation on the adoption or amendment of the Zoning
Ordinance.

Section 17.02.260.D of the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) stipulates that the Planning
Commission render its recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the
reasons for the recommendation, to the City Council.
Introduction/background:

Occasionally, it is necessary to update sections of the Zoning Code to make it consistent with
the City’s current uses, practices, and development patterns, and to update obsolete
development standards, to comply with State and Federal Law, to clarify ambiguous
requirements, and to streamline the review process to support housing development in the
 Norwalk Planning Commission  October 22, 2025
Zoning Text Amendment No. 2025-01  Page No. 2

City. Staff recommends amendments to Title 17 (“Zoning”) of the NMC to add a new Chapter
17.04.205 to Article “III” (“Accessory Buildings and Structures”); amend Section 17.04.210
(“Accessory Dwelling Units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units); and amend Chapter 17.05
(“Residential Zones”).

Accessory Dwelling Units

An Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) is a complete, independent living facility accessory to the
primary residence. In 2003, California adopted Assembly Bill (AB) 1866 to limit local
regulations from requiring a conditional use permit for second units to incentivize construction
of more housing as part of the State’s overall strategy in addressing the housing crisis. In
2016, the California Legislature also adopted California State Senate Bill (SB) 1069, AB
2299, and AB 2406 to govern ADUs and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs). Since
then, State ADU Laws have continued to evolve to lower barriers to the development of more
affordable housing including the most recent adoption of AB 2533 and SB 1211 that became
effective on January 1, 2025.

The Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) was last updated in 2018 to include ADU development
standards. However, with continued changes to State ADU laws, the NMC is out of
compliance with current State Laws. The City has been applying the standards established
under State Law (Government Code Sections 66310-66342) for the review of ADUs. In
October and November 2024, staff presented the Planning Commission and City Council
with an ADU study session to gather input for the amended ADU ordinance. The proposed
amended ADU ordinance reflects to the extent possible both Planning Commission and City
Council guidance.

Furthermore, the City's 6th Cycle Housing Element Update (HEU), adopted in February 2023,
lists Program 1.4 (Accessory Dwelling Units) as a housing program, which requires the City
to update the existing ADU ordinance for compliance with State law. The amended ordinance
aligns the City's regulations with State requirements and enhances the effectiveness of
processing ADU and JADU applications to promote affordable housing development in
Norwalk.
Proposed Zoning Code Amendments:

NMC Section 17.04.210 Accessory Dwelling Units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units

The proposed recommended updates to the NMC align the ordinance with State ADU law
requirements (Government Code Sections 66310-66342), ensuring compliance and
promoting efficient application processing of affordable housing development consistent with
the City’s Housing Element Update goals.

The ADU text amendment consists of the following components:
 Norwalk Planning Commission  October 22, 2025
Zoning Text Amendment No. 2025-01  Page No. 3

•  Establish definitions governing ADUs and JADUs in the NMC ADU Ordinance. The
  proposed text amendments will provide definitions specific to the regulations for ADUs and
  JADUs for clarification.
•  Allow for JADUs on lots with a single-family residence. Currently, JADUs are not a listed
  use in the NMC. The proposed ordinance update will include the definition and
  development standard requirements for proposed JADUs pursuant to Government Code
  section 66323.
•  Expand ADU uses to multifamily dwellings. Pursuant to Government Code section 66323,
  the City shall allow ADUs on lots with an existing or proposed multifamily primary dwelling.
  The proposed text amendments will establish the definition of "multifamily”, the number of
  ADUs allowed, and development standard requirements.
•  Update various portions of the ADU ordinance inconsistent with State ADU laws.
  Procedural and development standards for ADUs and JADUs are updated to reflect
  changes in legislation. Outdated regulations will be removed and replaced to be in
  compliant with State regulations. These regulations include, but are not limited to:
  application and review process, zoning, number of ADUs and JADUs allowed on single-
  family and multifamily residences, configuration and location, building height, setbacks,
  owner occupancy requirements, design standards, and off-street parking. The proposed
  updates to the City’s ADU ordinance will provide clear standards in reviewing ADUs and
  JADUs, promote architecturally compatible units within the City, and bring the ordinance
  into compliance with State ADU laws.

NMC Section 17.01.060, Section 17.05.205, and Chapter 17.05 Zoning Code Updates

The following zoning code amendments are recommended to amend various sections of the
zoning code by adding, removing or clarifying requirements. The recommended amendments
also ensure proper separation of buildings and neighborhood compatibility. In addition, the
recommended amendments aim to minimize health, safety and privacy concerns. The
recommended amendments include common and sound planning principals that are common
place in neighboring cities and intend to maintain quality of life in the City’s residential
neighborhoods.

Definitions (Section 17.01.060)
•  Delete duplicate ADU definition, revised definitions and provide illustrations for Floor Area
  Ratio, Building Height, and Lot Coverage, and add a definition for Top Plate Height.

Accessory Buildings and Structures (Section 17.05.205)
•  Add a new chapter to address development standards such as height, floor area, lot
  coverage, location, setbacks, design, and plumbing within accessory buildings. The
 Norwalk Planning Commission  October 22, 2025

  current zoning code lacks clarity and specific standards in regulating accessory buildings
  and structures in residential zones.

Residential Zones (NMC Chapter 17.05)
• Add accessory buildings and structures as a permitted use under Chapter 17.04.205;
• Revised height requirements and added top plate height requirements;
• Modified front, side, and rear yard requirements and added second story yard
  requirements and added distance between buildings requirement;
• Added lot coverage and floor area ratio (FAR) requirements;
• Added standards to improve the design of residential dwellings and require laundry
  facilities for each individual unit; and
• In R-3 and R-4, added standards to enhance the appearance of trash enclosures and
  deleted accessible unit requirements that can be addressed by the Building Code.

  17.04.210 Accessory Dwelling Units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units
  A. Purpose. The purpose of this section is to establish regulations governing Accessory
  Dwelling Units (ADUs) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs) in accordance
  with California Government Code Section 66310-66342, et seq., as amended from
  time to time, and other applicable state laws. This section is not intended to conflict
  with State Law and shall be interpreted to be compatible with state enactments.
  Facilitating the development of ADUs and JADUs will increase the availability of
  affordable housing to suit the variety of lifestyles and needs of the community, while
  mitigating impacts on traffic, utilities, and public health and safety and preserving the
  character of residential neighborhoods.

  B. Definitions. Words and terms as used in ADU and JADU regulations of this Section
  are defined as follows:

  “Accessory Dwelling Unit” or “ADU” means an attached or detached residential
  unit that provides complete independent living facilities for one (1) or more persons
  and is located on a lot with a proposed or existing primary residential unit. It shall
  include permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation and
  be located on the same parcel that the primary residential unit is or will be situated.
  An accessory dwelling unit can also be an efficiency unit, as defined in Section
  17958.1 of the Health and Safety Code, or a manufactured home, as defined in
  Section 18007 of the Health and Safety Code.

  “Accessory Building” or “Accessory Structure” means a detached structure that
  is accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the same lot.

  “Attached” means the ADU or Junior ADU shares a wall with the existing or proposed
  single dwelling or the multiple-family dwelling, with both sides of the wall being
  habitable space. ADUs or Junior ADUs shall not be connected to the existing or
  proposed single-family dwelling or multiple-family structure solely by a patio cover,
  breezeway or similar roofed area.

  “Building Height” means height is measured at existing legal grade to the peak of
  the structure.

  “Complete Independent Living Facilities” means permanent provisions for living,
  sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation on the same parcel as the single-family or
  multiple-family dwelling is or will be situated.

  “Detached” means the ADU is physically separated from the existing or proposed
  single dwelling or the multiple-family dwelling.

  “Efficiency Kitchen” means a kitchen that includes at a minimum:
  1. Appliances for cooking food and refrigeration, either built-in or countertop.
  2. A sink for food preparation greater than 12 inches by 12 inches, excluding the sink
  located in the bathroom.

a particular area where the keeping or maintaining of horses and other equine for the
personal use of members of the family residing on the property has become or is intended

§ 17.05.400. Permitted uses.

In an R-4 zone, no building shall be erected, constructed, reconstructed or structurally altered
or undergo substantial exterior remodel or parking modifications without the issuance and
approval of a precise development plan, pursuant to Section 17.02.240. Additions and
structural alterations which do not require the provision of additional parking spaces, are
architecturally compatible, and are consistent with Chapter 17.01, Article IV, may be
approved by the Director. The use of any building or land shall be used as specifically
provided and allowed by this article and Section 17.02.240.

In the R-4 zone, the following uses are permitted:
  A. Any use permitted in the R-3 zone under the same specified conditions,
  except that the following uses are not permitted:
  1.  Single room occupancy housing.
  B.  Multiple dwellings, including group houses, and boarding houses.
  C.  Accessory buildings and structures pursuant to the requirements of Section
  17.04.205.
  D.  An accessory dwelling unit pursuant to the requirements of Section 17.04.210.
  E.  Such other uses as are set forth in Chapter 17.04, upon the conditions therein
  provided.
  F.  The following, subject to the issuance, existence and validity of a conditional
  use permit as provided for in Section 17.02.210, and full compliance with each
  and every condition thereof:
  1.  Public playgrounds and parks;
  2.  Churches, synagogues, temples and other buildings, including related
  accessory uses, primarily devoted to religious worship;
  3.  Educational institutions;
  4.  Public utilities and public service uses or structures;
  5.  Multiple dwellings and other permitted buildings exceeding the height
  limit, if additional and compatible setbacks are provided so that adjacent
  buildings and properties are not dwarfed nor significantly affected;
  6.  Heights exceeding 15 feet in height for buildings and structures which
  encroach into the required side or rear setbacks.
  G. Parking, as provided by Chapter 17.03, Article II; and parking at different ratios
  may be established by the adoption of an official zoning plan.

§ 17.05.410. Building height.

  A.  No primary building or structure shall exceed two and one-half stories or 30 35 feet
  in height, whichever is the lesser; except multiple dwellings equipped with elevators
  and other permitted buildings if either is approved by conditional use permit; and
  except as provided by Section 17.03.230 for certain roof and similar structures.

  B.  The maximum allowable top plate height shall be 14 feet for the first story and 24
  feet for the second story. Notwithstanding other provisions of this chapter, three-
  story buildings, if less than 35 feet in height, are permitted if the buildings contain
  no more than two levels of separate occupancies with two-story dwelling units
  above the ground floor but entries and occupancies of the third floor level, which
  are separate from the second floor level, are expressly prohibited.

  C.  Buildings and structures which encroach into the required side or rear setbacks
  shall not exceed one story or 15 feet in height.

§ 17.05.420. Front setback.

  A.  Every lot and every parcel in an R-4 zone shall have a front setback from the front
  property line of not less than 15% of the lot depth, provided that such front setback
  depth need not exceed 15 feet for the first story. The second story shall be setback
  an additional five feet from the first story. and shall be equipped with an automatic
  irrigation system and landscaped and maintained in accordance with adopted City
  standards.

  B.  Greater front setbacks may be required by the Planning Commission.

  C.  Front setbacks shall be kept clear of any structures, except as specifically allowed
  in this title, and landscaped, as required by Section 17.03.010 and shall be
  equipped with an automatic irrigation system and landscaped and maintained in
  accordance with adopted City standards.

  D.  No structures, open storage, equipment, other than approved amenities or
  landscape feature, shall be maintained in unenclosed or open yard areas visible
  from abutting street(s), except as specifically allowed in this title.

§ 17.05.440. Rear setback.

  A. Every lot and parcel in the R-4 zone shall have a rear setback from the rear
  property line of not less than 20% of the lot depth but need not exceed 20 feet.
  B. Greater rear setbacks may be required by the Planning Commission.
  C. Front Rear setbacks shall be landscaped as required by Section 17.03.010.
  D. Rear setbacks shall be kept clear of any structures, except the following may
  be located within a rear setback:
  1. As specifically allowed in Chapter 17.03, Article IV.
  2. Approved residential driveways leading to a legal parking space.
  3. Amenities, as listed in Section 17.05.490(D), shall be screened from
  adjacent streets and properties, except that these amenities shall be
  screened from adjacent streets and properties.
  4. Garages, laundry facilities, storage, private balconies (but such balconies
  shall not be used for access) and similar uses within such structures may
  encroach into side setbacks from interior lot lines, except that these
  accessory uses shall maintain a minimum three-foot setback from rear
  property lines.
  5. Open automobile parking spaces when permitted upon Planning
  Commission approval.

 § 17.05.450. Area.

The minimum required area of a lot or parcel in the R-4 zone shall be 25,000 square feet.
Greater minimum required areas may be established for any lots or parcels by the adoption
of an official zoning plan. No development shall be permitted on any lot which does not meet
the minimum required area and does not meet the access requirements pursuant to Section
17.03.220.

§ 17.05.460. Lot width.

The minimum required width for any lot or parcel in the R-4 zone shall be 100 feet. Greater
minimum lot widths may be established for any lots or parcels by the adoption of an official
zoning plan. No development shall be permitted on any lot which does not meet the minimum
lot width and does not meet the access requirements pursuant to Section 17.03.220.

§ 17.05.462. Distance Between Buildings.

The minimum distance between all buildings and structures shall be 10 feet measured from
eave to eave.

§ 17.05.464. Lot Coverage.

The maximum allowable lot coverage shall not exceed 60 percent of the lot size.

§ 17.05.466. Floor Area Ratio.

The maximum allowable floor area ratio shall not exceed 60 percent of lot the size.

§ 17.05.470. Density.

The allowable density for every lot or parcel in the R-4 zone shall be between 23 and 30
dwelling units per acre.

§ 17.05.480. Open space.

Every lot in the R-4 zone which is used for multiple dwelling uses shall contain a minimum of
500 square feet of usable open space or shall conform to the requirements herein after
specified, whichever is greater.
  A. Minimum Open Space Required.
  1. Units with one bedroom or less: 200 square feet per unit, with at least 50
  square feet of this open space must be private usable open space for each
  unit.
  2. Units with two bedrooms: 300 square feet per unit, with at least 50 square feet
  of this open space must be private usable open space for each unit.
  3. Units with three bedrooms or more: 400 square feet per unit, with at least 50
  square feet of this open space must be private usable open space for each
  unit.
  4. Townhouses and Condominiums. Additional open area may be required upon
  precise development plan review.
  B. Standards.

§ 17.05.490. Landscaping, architectural and building design standards.

Every development in the R-4 zone shall conform to the following provisions which are
considered desirable development standards reflecting the spirit and intent of the multiple-
family residential zone. Developments shall incorporate these standards using quality
building materials to the maximum extent possible.
  A. Full Site Development. To the maximum extent possible all new construction
  shall encompass the entire site and partial development incorporating existing
  structures is discouraged.
  B. Landscaping shall be provided as required by Chapter 17.03, Article I.
  C. Architectural Elements. Developments shall incorporate the following
  architectural elements using quality building materials to the maximum extent
  possible:
  1. Multi-level roof lines.
  2. Private entries for each unit.
  3. Covered entries for each unit.
  4. Exterior trim, including, but not limited to, wood siding, brick, stone,
  slumpstone, or other decorative treatments.
  5. Windows recessed a minimum of three inches.
  6. Varied exterior building materials.
  7. Architectural quality roofing material, siding material, entry doors,
  windows, and garage doors. Asphalt composition shingles do not
  constitute architectural quality roofing material. The materials shall be
  subject to the approval of the Director.
  8. Concrete areas shall incorporate a stamped or stained pattern within the
  parking and circulation areas.
  9. All developments of five or more units shall incorporate an entry kiosk for
  pedestrian access into the project.
  10. Building elevations visible from public view shall be enhanced through the
  incorporation of reveals, recesses, trim elements, and other architectural
  design features to provide articulation and visual interest to the
  streetscape.

  F.  Waste, Garbage and Trash Regulations.
  1. All developments must have trash storage areas which shall be located
  for the convenience of the residents and for efficiency of collection. One
  six-foot by eight-foot enclosure is required at the ratio of one for every five
  units for the purpose of storing garbage, waste, refuse and trash. Such
  enclosure shall have on each side thereof a solid reinforced masonry wall
  of not less than five feet in height except for openings. All openings shall
  be equipped with solid, view-obscuring gates or doors which meet the
  height requirement of this section and the fence requirements for
  durability. Such gates or doors shall be equipped at all times with a fully
  operating, self-closing device. At least one opening or gate or door shall
  be of sufficient width to provide reasonable and necessary access to the
  storage area and such opening door or gate shall at all times be located
  and maintained at such a place and in such a fashion that access to the
  storage area for the deposit and removal of waste, trash, refuse and
  garbage is reasonably afforded. A roof shall be provided for the trash
  enclosure. The Director may approve substitution of a solid fence or other
  material when such fence or other material will adequately comply with
  the provision of this section.
  2. The finish and color of the enclosure, gate and roof shall be decorative
  and shall incorporate primary elements from the site building style. Chain
  link and or vinyl fencing shall not be permitted.
  3. All garbage stored within such enclosure shall be placed and maintained
  in a metal or plastic container which has an overlapping fly-tight lid. The
